conflicts.fact: Median of Mama Wanjiku's five-day ugali data (and the dataset itself)
conflicts.versions: Phenomenon: median is 57. Lesson 3: data 54, 60, 57, 60, 59, ordered 54, 57, 59, 60, 60, median = 59 (but the overview says 58 and its Explain/Model phases use 59). Lesson 6: data 55, 60, 58, 60, 57 (median would be 58). Lesson 7/8: median = 57 with mean 58 and mode 60, and Lesson 7 uses a 7-day dataset.

conflicts.fact: Daily ugali sales dataset for the same week
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3: 54, 60, 57, 60, 59 (sum 290). Lesson 5: 54, 60, 55, 62, 59 (sum 290 only by coincidence, mean 58, no repeated 60). Lesson 6: 55, 60, 58, 60, 57. Lesson 7: seven days 54, 60, 57, 62, 55, 58, 60 (sum 406, mean 58). Same 'week' of data changes between lessons.

conflicts.fact: Total number of orders and ugali's share
conflicts.versions: Phenomenon, Lessons 1, 2, 4, 8: 120 learners/orders, ugali ~47% (4: around 55–60 of 120). Lesson 5: frequency table totals 150 orders (ugali 56, 37%), and Lesson 5's frequencies sum to 150 and give 37%, contradicting 47%.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the mean/mode/median were taught and numbering of lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 teaches mean, mode and median together; Lessons 6 and 7 teach mean/mode and median again as new, and Lesson 7 says mean was calculated in Lesson 5 and mode added in Lesson 6; Lesson 4 says mean is bridged to Lesson 5; Lesson 6 says mean/mode, with median as a new open question.

conflicts.fact: What the frequency table / data collected in earlier lessons contained
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the frequency table from Lesson 2 contains the daily ugali totals; Lesson 2 only collected students' own surveys (meal, transport, sport) and did not build a frequency table (Lesson 4 does).

Lesson 6 states Kericho mean = 147.5 mm/month, but its data (71, 91, 193, 276, 216, 38) sum to 885, giving a mean of 147.5, which is consistent; however it claims 'no mode' while Lesson 3 treats mode as the most common value, and Lesson 3 says the mode of the daily totals is 'peak demand day'. Lesson 6 calls mode 'most common single-day demand' for stock ordering.
